name: Oxidized
what_it_is: Oxidized is a network device configuration backup tool and modern RANCID replacement that automatically retrieves and versions configurations from 130+ network OS types. It provides Git-based versioning, a REST API, syslog-driven change detection, and an extensible hook system for notifications.
components: Threading engine for parallel device retrieval (auto-scales thread count to meet configured interval)
REST API server for node management and configuration fetching
Syslog UDP/file listener for change-event capture with user attribution
YAML configuration parser with layered merge (system-wide + user-specific)
Hook system for external integrations (Exec, GitHub, AWS SNS, Slack, XMPP, Cisco Spark/Webex)
measurement: Version history and diffs via REST API (/node/version)
Git blame tracks which user triggered configuration changes
Syslog events capture config-change timestamps and user attribution
configuration: Primary config file: /etc/oxidized/config (YAML) or ~/.config/oxidized/config, merged in order
OXIDIZED_HOME env var overrides default config directory
Sources configurable: CSV (RANCID router.db), SQLite, MySQL, HTTP endpoint
Outputs configurable: file, Git, Git-Crypt, HTTP POST
Credentials and privileged-mode access defined per model or group
Threading interval and concurrency tunable in YAML config
fault_injection: No native fault-injection or chaos capabilities documented
Hook system (Exec hook) can run arbitrary commands on events, enabling external fault triggers
Syslog listener can be targeted with synthetic syslog messages to simulate config-change events
modes: Continuous polling mode (default): retrieves configs on a recurring interval
Priority queue mode: PUT /node/next/[NODE] moves a node to the head of the queue
Daemon mode with systemd service file provided
constraints: Must NOT be run as root; a dedicated non-root system user is required
Requires Ruby runtime and optional gems for web UI and script extensions
Supported only on Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+, Rocky Linux 9+, RHEL, Fedora, FreeBSD 14.2+ (or from source)
No documented hard cap on concurrent devices, but thread count must be tuned to meet retrieval interval
Git output backend requires a pre-initialized Git repository accessible by the oxidized user
docker_services: Docker and Podman deployment supported (referenced in README as documented separately); no docker-compose.yml found in repository root
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in repository root (404 on fetch)
No built-in metrics or Prometheus endpoint
No native fault-injection or network simulation capabilities
No TLS/HTTPS on the REST API documented natively
No scalability benchmarks or hard concurrency limits documented
No built-in backup recovery or restore workflow documented
